newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila warns Congo opposition to stop protests.
newsitem.headline: Kabila warns Congo opposition to stop protests.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila on Sunday reminded opposition leaders that political activity was banned in new Congo and he held them responsible for injuries sustained by demonstrators as a march was dispersed last week.

"Political activity as well as political demonstrations have been banned during the transition. Political leaders have to comply with the law," he told a news conference at the end of a visit by Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa.
"March organisers are to be held responsible for those who are shot so that the peace can be kept," he added.

On Friday a march by up to 1,000 supporters of the PALU opposition party through the centre of Kinshasa to protest against the ban on political activity was violently dispersed by soldiers who opened fire into the crowd.
Witnesses said three people were killed and five injured, but Interior Minister Mwenze Kongolo dismissed the figures as "untrue". Four people were hurt, but no one was killed, he said.
Kabila declared himself president with sweeping powers in May after a seven-month bush war.
His Alliance forces have broken up many peaceful demonstrations, sometimes opening fire without warning.
He said at the news conference that opposition politicians did not participate in the liberation struggle, and that they were more in favour of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
"Leaders can come and meet me at any time, but they don't have to stage demonstration protests to put to the test our ability to keep the peace," he said.
